Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual voucher activity — Nebula Systems

Hi Jordan / Ben —

We flagged a cluster of promotional voucher redemptions tied to "Nebula Systems" across five separate accounts in the last 30 days. Key signals: repeated voucher codes reused from the same IPv4 range, overlapping phone numbers that differ by one digit, and multiple requests for additional promotional grants after expiration.

I've attached an excerpt from the audit logs showing the account ids, IPs, and timestamps for the redemptions. Nothing here conclusively proves fraud, but the pattern matches previously observed scripted voucher claims.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Pause issuance of any further promotional credits to related accounts.
- Ask Nebula for clarification about multiple signups / teams (POs etc.).
- If Nebula cannot verify, consider flagging accounts for temporary suspension and reclaiming grants.

Attachment: audit-log-excerpt.csv (rows 1-50)

—Naomi

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for taking the quick ping. We noticed several separate accounts redeeming the same promotional vouchers and then requesting top-ups within a short window. Before we move forward with any additional grants, can you confirm whether those signups were legitimate distinct teams within Nebula (e.g., R&D, CloudOps, Internal PoC)? If possible please:

- Share the internal approval or PO that authorized multiple signups (PDF is fine).
- Confirm whether the teams are separate legal entities or internal subteams.
- Let us know if any single person manages multiple accounts.

For now we're pausing additional promotional allocations historically granted to the Nebula org until we validate. If this is causing an active POC to stall, I'm happy to schedule a 20-min call to sort through the details.

Next steps from our side: Naomi will run a deeper log correlation and Ben will pull any previous promo exceptions on file.

Best,

Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the heads up. Nebula runs several small, semi-autonomous teams and we recently spun up parallel PoCs in three business units; each team requested its own sandbox account. That's likely the cause. I'm attaching our internal PO and a short note from procurement confirming authorization.

Two quick clarifications:
- The teams are not separate legal entities — all under Nebula Systems, same billing entity.
- We did not intentionally try to game promotions; different engineers signed up for speed.

Can you let us know what evidence you need to reinstate the paused promos? We're happy to consolidate under a single billing account if that's required.

Attachment: nebula-purchase-order.pdf

Regards,

Team —

Thanks for the investigation and the PO from Nebula. A few points from policy & next steps: 

1) Policy baseline: Redwood promotional vouchers are intended for single-team evaluation per org unless explicitly approved by Sales with documented exception. Multiple parallel sandbox signups under the same billing entity are allowed only when procurement provides a consolidated request and Sales logs an exception.

2) Evidence review: The PO partially explains parallel PoCs but does not address the IP/phone-number clustering nor the repeated voucher reclaims. Naomi, please correlate the purchase order rows against the redemption IPs and flag any accounts that still look automated.

3) Immediate action: Temporarily suspend additional promotional grants to the related account group and mark deal HB-2247 as "on hold for compliance" in CRM. Jordan/Ben, reach back to Nebula and offer two options: (A) consolidate the teams under one billing account and we'll reissue a controlled promo pool, or (B) provide per-team written authorization on company letterhead for separate promos — otherwise we deny further vouchers.

4) If we see evidence of deliberate coupon-cycling or proxy automation, escalate to Legal for recovery and reclaiming prior grants.

Please confirm you have the action items and copy the HubSpot record HS-523764 for updates.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
